title: Treasury and Liquidity
answer: Cash forecasting, currency hedging, idle cash, bank reconciliation and stress testing.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Cash Flow Forecasting
children.blurb: Cash flow forecasting is the practice of estimating when money will actually arrive and when it must go out, usually over the next thirteen weeks and again over the coming year.

children.name: Currency Hedging
children.blurb: Currency hedging covers the practice of using financial instruments to offset the effect of exchange rate movements on a company's cash flows, balance sheet, or forecast transactions.

children.name: Idle Cash and Short-Term Yield
children.blurb: Idle cash and short-term yield covers the management of operating balances that are not needed for near-term obligations, and the instruments used to earn a return on them.

children.name: Bank Reconciliation
children.blurb: Bank reconciliation is the process of matching a company's internal cash records against the bank's statement and explaining every difference between the two.

children.name: Liquidity Stress Testing
children.blurb: Liquidity stress testing is the practice of modelling whether a firm can meet its cash and collateral obligations under adverse conditions, such as deposit runs, frozen wholesale funding markets or a ratings downgrade.

sections.body: Treasury and liquidity work is where artificial intelligence is being used to predict cash movements, manage currency exposure, and keep accounts matched against bank records. In cash forecasting, models read payment histories, invoice timing, and payroll cycles to produce daily or weekly projections that a treasurer can adjust. Currency hedging tools watch exposure across accounts and suggest when a forward contract or option might offset a swing. Idle cash systems scan balances across banks and flag amounts that could be moved into short term instruments. Bank reconciliation uses matching algorithms to pair ledger entries with bank statements and isolate the exceptions that need a person. Stress testing runs scenarios against the cash position to show how it would hold up under a shock.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Reconciliation is the most mature area, because matching two lists of transactions is a bounded problem and the models have years of labeled data to learn from. Forecasting is harder, since cash behavior depends on customer decisions, supplier terms, and one off events that no historical pattern fully captures, so most systems produce a range rather than a single number. Hedging and idle cash work sit in a middle zone where the software can surface options and exposures but the decision still belongs to a human with a mandate. Stress testing is often the least automated, because scenario design is judgment heavy and regulators want to see the assumptions behind the numbers. The honest limit across all five is that these tools see the data they are given, and a missed account or a delayed feed will quietly distort every projection built on top of it.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader new to the area should start with Cash Flow Forecasting, which sets out the core problem of predicting inflows and outflows and explains why accuracy degrades as the horizon stretches. Currency Hedging follows naturally for anyone whose cash sits in more than one currency, covering exposure measurement and how models rank possible hedges. Idle Cash and Short-Term Yield takes the same balance data and asks a different question, namely which funds are sitting still and what instruments might be available for them. Bank Reconciliation is the practical counterpart, showing how the ledger and the bank statement get matched and where human review is still required. Liquidity Stress Testing closes the section by taking the forecasts, the hedges, and the reconciled balances and running them through adverse scenarios, which is where the weaknesses in the earlier steps tend to show up.
